Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can move to legal:

- We showed Clinix's sample workflows (diagnostic intake -> prompt -> model output). Our legal/compliance team needs explicit answers on what Redwood stores by default and what we can opt into.
- Can you confirm the default behavior for: (a) raw prompts (inputs), (b) model outputs (generated text), (c) derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks), and (d) KV/prefix cache?
- What are the default retention windows for request logs and request payloads? Is there an immutable audit trail available?
- Residency: we need EU data residency for all stored artifacts if we enable storage. Is that supportable for a pilot (we're running a mixed US/EU test but want EU-only for EU patient data)?
- Encryption & keys: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for stored artifacts and audit logs?
- Evidence: please attach SOC 2 attestation and a simple architecture diagram showing where prompt/outputs/telemetry live.

We're considering enabling a short-term storage option for outputs for an experimental pilot — likely 180 days. If that's possible, legal will want an addendum or DPA language.

Next steps: can you send a short written confirmation (bullet list) of defaults + opt-in options and the DPA draft? Also please loop in engineering/security for any technical clarifications.

Attaching: POC_scope.xlsx (high level).

Thanks,
Samira

Hi Samira —

Great talking earlier. Below is a concise summary of Redwood defaults and the opt-in paths so legal/engineering at Clinix can review quickly. Lauren and Dev are cc'd for the technical/security specifics (they'll add a config snippet).

High-level (defaults for Redwood Hosted API):
- Prompt inputs: not persisted by default. Transient in-memory processing; we do not write raw prompts to long-term storage unless a customer explicitly enables request logging.
- Model outputs: not stored by default. Generated text is returned to the caller and garbage-collected; persistent storage only when opt-in for session/archive storage is enabled.
- Embeddings/reranks: not saved unless you opt into the embeddings store (explicit API/console toggle).
- KV / prefix cache: in-memory only for serving performance; not materialized to disk in hosted mode.
- Logs/telemetry: request metadata and anonymized telemetry are retained by default for 30 days. These logs are encrypted at rest and used for SLO/debugging and billing.

Options / enterprise controls:
- Retention window: for Hosted customers default logs = 30 days. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can configure custom retention (30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days) and retention policies can be added as an addendum.
- Residency: EU residency is supported via our Private deployment or by provisioning Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1. Hosted EU-region placement is also available for certain plans — we'll confirm based on your contract tier.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS) supported in Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for enterprise tiers.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trail options available for Dedicated/Private; hosted has standard request logs with retention controls.

Attachments (initial): data_processing_map.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf, DPA_Draft.docx

If Clinix needs 180 days for a pilot: we can do that via an addendum (legal) and a config flag in the tenant to enable output persistence + 180-day TTL. Lauren will provide the precise flag names and a sample config. Dev will confirm encryption and KV disk guarantees.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tuesday (Oct 19) with legal + engineering to review the DPA draft and confirm deployment path. Does that work?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Samira — following Marcus's summary, a few technical clarifications and sample configs so your engineers can validate behavior quickly. Quoting Marcus for context:

> - Prompt inputs: not persisted by default...
> - Model outputs: not stored by default...

Technical details (hosted behavior unless otherwise configured):
- Request handling: prompts and outputs are processed in-memory by the serving runtime. There is no default write-to-disk of prompt text or output text.
- KV / prefix cache: strictly in-memory. Evicted caches are never flushed to persistent volumes in hosted mode.
- Request logs: we persist request metadata (timestamps, route, model id, token counts, errors) and a hashed request id for tracing. By default we do NOT persist raw prompt text or raw model outputs in the request logs.
- Telemetry & debug traces: when a customer enables "request logging" the raw payload is stored in a secured store; this is an explicit opt-in and appears in the tenant settings.
- Embeddings: not written to embeddings store unless you call the embeddings API and also have "persist_embeddings: true" set. If persisting, retention_days is configurable (sample values: 90, 180, 365).
- Encryption: stored artifacts (logs, embeddings, persisted outputs) are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Dedicated/Private can be configured with customer KMS.
- Audit trail: we can enable append-only audit logs in Dedicated/Private (suitable for compliance). Hosted audit logs are available but with standard retention controls (30 days by default).

Sample config snippet (for opt-in persistent outputs + 180d TTL):

--- config.yaml ---
tenant_settings:
  persist_outputs: true  # default: false
  output_retention_days: 180
  persist_embeddings: false
  embeddings_retention_days: 90
  region_override: eu-west-1  # optional: force EU residency for stored artifacts
--------------------

Notes: enabling persist_outputs will cause prompts/outputs to be written to an encrypted object store for the TTL period. For EU residency we must provision an EU-backed tenant (Private or Dedicated) or use hosted EU tenancy if available for your tier.

I'll attach a lightweight config example and a one-page architecture diagram that highlights where data lands.

Thanks — happy to jump on the Tue call to walk through the config and DPA language.

Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
